normalized_claim: For every prime p, natural s,M with M>2s, e solved coordinates and k parameter coordinates, F,H in Z_p[Y,T]^e and a=(y0,t0) an exact root of F, let J=D_Y F(a), K=D_T F(a). Assume J invertible over Q_p and p^s J^{-1} integral. For every v in Z_p^k prescribe tau=t0+p^M v and G=F+p^M H. Construct the unique y in y0+p^(s+1) Z_p^e satisfying G(y,tau)=0. Prove y-y0 in p^(M-s) Z_p^e and y-y0=-p^M J^{-1}(H(a)+K v)+epsilon with integral epsilon in p^(2M-3s) Z_p^e. No assumption on the perturbed Jacobian; retain the same exponent s. Arbitrary p-adic coefficients and centers, all primes including 2, and zero finite dimensions.
critical_implications: Actual augmented polynomials are (F,T-t0) and (H,-v), and their perturbed root equation is equivalent to the original perturbed equation and exact T=t0+p^M v.
Actual evaluated partial derivatives give B=[[J,K],[0,I]]. No unrelated supplied Jacobian stands in for it.
Original p^s J^-1 integrality gives AJ=JA=p^s I. C=[[A,-AK],[0,p^s I]] gives CB=BC=p^s I with the same s.
The inherited contraction normalization constructs an actual augmented perturbed root and retains depth M-s without assuming the new Jacobian is invertible.
The integral first-order estimate applies to the constructed root. Its solved projection has force A(H(a)+Kv), with the plus sign fixed by two negatives.
Original solved inverse conversion yields the rational formula with an integral error of depth 2M-3s.
Every competing solved root in y0+p^(s+1) has full joined point in a+p^(s+1), since M>=s+1. Thus uniqueness has the stated entire solved-ball scope.
